newsitem.title: USA: American Waste says seeking arbitration.
newsitem.headline: American Waste says seeking arbitration.

text.p: American Waste Services Inc said on Monday it had filed a demand for arbitration regarding a remediation project in Denver, Colorado.

The company said it is claiming that its customer is in default and has materially breached its payment obligation in the case. It also said that an arbitration hearing date had been scheduled for the third quarter of 1997.
American Waste Services did not name the customer in question.

The company also said it had incurred significant costs in the first quarter of 1997 as a result of a stop work order issued by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency from January 22 until March 20 at the site.
It added that the customer had subsequently filed a counter claim alleging the company has refused to proceed with the work outlined in its contract.
The customer hired another contractor to complete the project, American Waste Services said.
"An unfavorable resolution could have a material negative effect on the company's future financial results," American Waste Services said of the case.
American Waste Services Inc provides waste management and environmental services, including disposal and transportation services.
